text: You can now learn Old Testament verses by heart in Hebrew, read right to left, saying or typing them and being checked on the letters.
The Weave's Order setting now says "Original" instead of "Greek", and the Weave, Read lessons and Quiz goal descriptions say Greek or Hebrew.
You can now learn the IPA sounds of Hebrew too, as an optional lesson on the Goal screen, and a new IPA lesson setting turns the optional lessons off.
The Hebrew lessons now go past the letters to nouns, pronouns, prepositions, verbs and sentences, twenty-six new cards with words from Genesis 1 and Jonah 1.

One Pronunciation setting now covers both Greek and Hebrew, with a switch to set each on its own, Hebrew gets its own voice, speed and keyboard settings, and a Hebrew word's sheet shows how it sounds in English letters.
In Turn pages, a chapter's last page no longer comes out blank when the Maps button fell just past the end of the text.
You can now learn the Hebrew letters in Lampas, with a card, a sound lesson and a drill for each one, and the other reading marks have cards too.
The Verse view now shows an Old Testament verse in Hebrew, right to left, and Listen reads it in a Hebrew voice, when you open it from the Hebrew view.
The Goal and Placement screens now work for Hebrew, with a Greek | Hebrew switch when you read both, and The Hebrew alphabet can be learned or marked known there.
Old Testament chapters now follow the "How much Hebrew?" setting and New Testament chapters follow "How much Greek?", including the word sheet, the study resources and what the tutor is told.
Settings now ask which languages you read (English only, Greek, Hebrew or both) and give Hebrew its own "How much Hebrew?" dial beside the Greek one.
Your requests now says when each request was sent, filed, built or answered, and tells you when one has been waiting in the queue for over a week.
The sentence-diagram lesson has a tenth step that names each line of a diagram by its Greek grammar term, and each term opens its own lesson.
Review now asks how well you knew a word, Know it well, Kind of or Don't know, and brings it back sooner or later to match.
Your requests can be filtered by Waiting, Adopted or Declined, with a count on each.
when you ask the tutor about a map, it can now also link you to the Logos Atlas, which opens in your own Logos.

the lessons on the conjunction, the article, the adjective, the pronoun, the preposition, the verb, the infinitive, the participle and the adverb each draw a short verse as a sentence diagram, with the word they teach lit.
the sentence diagram of Colossians 3:2 hangs "not" (μὴ) on "the things on earth", not on "Set your minds", and the wrong diagram kept on your phone is not shown again: it is worked out afresh once.
Lampas now checks that you really know an idea you once missed by asking you a new question on it, and Drill it only proves an idea on questions you have not been asked before.
the lessons on the noun and on the nominative, accusative, genitive and dative cases now draw a short verse as a sentence diagram, with the word the lesson teaches lit.
Tap any request on Your requests to read it in full, with the date of its latest news and its tracking number; asks you send from now on keep your own words.
The small link words (ὅτι, γάρ, οὖν, δέ, ἀλλά and the rest) now have memory pictures, one family of two bars and a link drawn differently for each, so you can tell them apart.
With Logos on, the Maps sheet now has a Logos Atlas block that opens the atlas map for the verse, centred on its places, and your Lexham Geographic Commentary at the passage, in Logos.
Drill it and the short drill now use the extra questions the tutor writes for the ideas you miss, and never ask you the same one twice.
Under every sentence diagram a quiet "How to read this" opens the diagram lesson, and until you have finished or dismissed it, the first diagrams you open invite you to learn to read one.
Settings now has a Maps section with an On/Off switch for each source of maps, ready for a second atlas to sit beside Bible Mapper.
Holding a section heading or the line under the chapter now copies its passage or the whole chapter, in the format chosen under When you copy.
Copy now gives the verse the way you are reading it, English, Greek, Hebrew or the Weave, and Settings > Reading > Copy: text has a new choice, As you read it, which is the default.
An optional lesson, How to read a sentence diagram, teaches the lines of a sentence diagram one at a time on real verses, with a tap to check each.
Ask the tutor for a map of the verse you are reading and it answers with a Map button that opens the right map.

Copy in the verse view now copies the verse, passage or chapter with its reference, and you choose in Settings what it includes: English, the Greek or Hebrew, or both, the reference, verse numbers and the link.
The tutor can now take you to any chapter of the Bible, Old Testament as well as New, when you ask it to.
The Maps sheet for a verse now puts the maps that show the places named in that verse first, with those places listed under each map.
The About you screen now asks about any Greek or Hebrew you have had before, and the Hebrew word meanings for Jonah's great fish and the verb "appointed" are right.
Chapters and verses now show a quiet Maps button that opens Bible Mapper's maps for the place, each with its dates, credit and a link back to the site.
tapping one word of a phrase in the English text now looks up just that word in the dictionary, while the Greek or Hebrew word on the card stays the same.
In a window a third of the screen tall (split-screen), the Talk bar, the question box under Ask the tutor and a reference card's Play and Open are no longer cut off at the bottom.
Ask the tutor on an Old Testament verse now sees the Hebrew words of the verse, with their dictionary form, meaning and grammar, and can answer about them.
Tap a Hebrew word in an Old Testament chapter and see its sheet, with its meaning, grammar, Strong's number, sound and links to your Hebrew lexicons in Logos.
with the Audio Bible on and the text at its largest, the "Listen in Audible" link is no longer cut off by the Play button.
when you ask the Bible talk what an English word like "love" really means, the tutor now reliably answers in English and offers the Greek word as a button.
Old Testament chapters can now be read in the Hebrew, right to left, with every word tappable, and read aloud in Hebrew.
Your Old Testament and whole-Bible commentaries from Logos now open at an Old Testament verse, under "In another book…".
In a short split-screen window the reading screen's top no longer overlaps itself, and the Play button and gear stay on the same line as the title.
Old Testament verses now open in the Verse view, in English, and links, lists and memorizing work for them.
You can now read the whole Old Testament in English in Lampas, tap an English word to look it up, listen to it, and carry straight on from Malachi into Matthew.
The sentence diagram now follows the Weave, so a word the Weave shows in Greek is drawn in Greek in the diagram.
Your Logos library now opens several hundred more of your New Testament commentaries (every series in your list) from Lampas, searchable, at the verse you are reading.
The Library now lists all your Lenski, Baker, Pillar and NIGTC commentaries (and your interlinears and more Bibles), and its search says "commentaries" properly.
The verse screen has a Diagram button that has the tutor draw the verse as a sentence diagram you can slide sideways and tap any word of.
When the tutor helps you fill in a form you can now answer it by holding to talk, typing, or attaching or taking a photo, the same way you ask it about a verse.
From any talk with the tutor, and from the Ask on a verse, you can send the makers a request with Send to the makers, with pictures or a photo and your words.
Ask the tutor to take you to one of your verse lists by name, and Back brings you back to the talk.
Sending an ask to the makers from a talk now sends the pictures you attached to it, and Your requests shows how many went.
Saving the Bible references from a shared message as a list now has "Let the tutor do it", so the tutor can ask which list and what name and save them when you tap Send.
Ask for another approach and Ask for more now have a button, Let the tutor do it, that asks you the questions and fills in the form for you.
Quiz me on a whole chapter now sends the tutor whole verses from the start, not a text cut off mid-sentence.
Ask for a book (and Ask for another approach) now has "Let the tutor do it", where the tutor asks you in a talk, fills in the form as you answer and ends with a Send button for you to tap.
the tutor now knows which verses you are memorizing, can start memorizing one when you ask, and you can choose to send your memorizing progress with an Ask for more.
About now says when the tutor last tuned what it looks up for you, and why.

When you ask the tutor for something in the app, you now see what it is doing: a short line while it looks something up, a line with Undo for a change it makes, and Back brings you back to your talk after it takes you to another screen.
Today now has a Memorize piece that tells you how many verses are due and starts the first one with a tap; you can switch it off in Settings under Daily.
Your Logos library, with your Verse lists, is now the first thing in Settings instead of two taps down.
When the tutor takes you to another chapter, the phone's Back now brings you back to your talk with the tutor, as you left it.
Memorize is now a screen of its own, reached from the Library, showing the verses due today and every verse you are learning with how far along each is.
an error message and its Retry button stay on screen when you open a verse again after a question failed, even with the phone held sideways.
Memorize lets you type a verse from memory, in English always and in Greek once you turn on Greek keyboard in Settings.
Held sideways, the Listen screen shows the Listen in Audible link above the Play button again instead of pushing it out of sight.
When the tutor helps fill in a form, it now asks only about the required fields (the photo question aside) and never nags about the optional ones.
You can mark a Bible verse, or a whole verse list, to learn by heart, in English first and in Greek or the Weave if your Greek setting allows.
Accordance is no longer offered in Settings or on a word's sheet; if you want it, ask for it in Settings > More > Ask for more.
Words that have a note on their heart now show it on the word's sheet, on the card that first teaches the word, and after you miss it in Review, and the tutor is told the same note.
In a verse list's Edit you can move or copy a reference to another list, or to a new list you name on the spot.
Play and Play all now say the book, chapter and verse of each New Testament reference before reading it.
the Share to Lampas sheet no longer stays scrolled with its buttons out of view and a large blank space under the references.

in a Bible talk the tutor can ask for the passage the talk is heading toward; your phone reads its Greek and English in the background, a quiet 'Tutor fetched ...' line says so, and the tutor has it from your next question on.
Under Read more on an idea sheet, the grammars you pinned now come first, then the others.
A list of Bible references, and the references you share to Lampas, can be played aloud in order with a bar to pause or stop, skipping Old Testament ones with a spoken note.
When you ask about a verse in a chapter talk, the tutor now has that verse's text and says which verses it holds instead of going by memory.
Your requests are now grouped by kind with a count on each group, and a search box appears once you have more than twenty.
Ask the makers for a book from one place, picking it from your imported Logos list or typing its title, and send your whole list of books Lampas could open in one tap.
A verse list can now be edited: add a reference by typing it, remove one, move one up or down, or sort the list into Bible order.
Words you had already learned, like ἔρχομαι, now show their aorist form in Review and the word list, as new words do.
Lampas now says a licence covers up to five devices, not three.
On the Share to Lampas sheet, "Save as a list" keeps the Bible references you were shown, in the order you chose, as a new verse list or adds them to one you already have.
After a Review ending card, See the table opens the table on that very word's own forms, with the cell you were asked lit.
Lampas has a Verse lists screen under the Library for lists of Bible references you save, where you can open, rename and delete them (with Undo).
pressing Pause between two passages in the reference pop-up's reading now holds the next passage instead of letting it start.
The Greek verbs whose past tense cannot be guessed (come, see, eat, take, find, become and others) now show that form next to their meaning, like 'to come/go (aorist ἦλθον)'.
You can share your Logos list straight to Lampas from Files or Drive to import your library, without choosing the file inside the app.
Tapping Play in a Bible reference's pop-up reads the passage aloud, with Pause and Stop; an Old Testament reference says that no Old Testament is present.
You can import your Logos library from the spreadsheet Logos saves, and Lampas turns on every book it can open and says what it cannot use and why.
Ask the tutor "what's on my drill today?" and it names what Today holds for you and offers to open Today.

Settings no longer lists your Logos books; one line shows how many are on and opens Your Logos library, Bible in Logos and the daily devotional picker follow it, and the Settings search finds a book by its title.
The word sheet now shows just the lexicons you pinned, with a button "All N lexicons" that opens a searchable list of every lexicon you have on.
A verse now has In Logos and In another book…, which lists your Greek texts and commentaries that cover it, so you can open the verse in any of them.
A new Your Logos library screen lists the Logos books Lampas can open, by kind, where you switch each one off, on or pin it, and search by title or author.
the Bible talk tutor now gives a plain English answer, with one offer of the Greek, when you ask what an English word like "love" really means, and keeps its notes on a long talk.
Study resources now follow How much Greek?: at Just English the Greek ones are hidden, and at the steps between the English ones come first.
a picture you send to the tutor now opens full screen on top of everything, even over Drill it, and you can pinch to zoom it.
Tap an English word in Just English mode and a small sheet lets you hear it and look it up in Webster's 1828 dictionary in Logos.
after a lost connection, retrying the first message of a Bible talk no longer makes the tutor lose the thread of the conversation.
The tutor now keeps one thread through a whole talk, and when a long talk has to start its thread again it writes down the key points so far, which you can read under its answer.
After you change chapter by swiping, Lampas offers once to hide the chapter buttons at the end of a chapter, and Settings can bring them back.
A long talk with the tutor now remembers what you said at the start, instead of wandering after ten turns.
A table opened from a word can now show that word's own forms from the New Testament, with 'not in the NT' for forms it never uses, and a tap on a form shows where it is first used and opens it.

The play button now always reads on from where you are, to the end of the book or the end of the Bible as you choose in Settings; to hear less, play a verse, a section heading or the chapter from the bottom line.
Conversations, under Settings, lists every talk you have had with the tutor, with a search for any word and a tap to carry on where you left off.
The "How it sounds" note for pairs of words told apart by a mark now says that ἀλλά/ἄλλα and αὐτή/αὕτη are said with the stress on different syllables, instead of saying every pair sounds the same.
Settings help is easier to read: the Greek dial's six steps and other lists of choices are now lines with bold names.

Ask the tutor is one tap away on the Paradigms list and on every table, it opens over the table you are on, and the tutor already knows the table, whether you are in Learn or Drill, the form you tapped and the word you came from.
Tapping the place line at the foot of 2 John now names 2 John, not 2 John and 3 John.

On a paradigm table you can Learn (every form shown) or Drill (blank cells you tap and mark Had it or Missed, with a score and Drill the missed again at the end), and a setting How much of a table (Any, Solid and frontier, Solid only) chooses which forms are shown, in Settings and in the table's header.
A link to a book in your Logos library now opens it where the tutor says the topic is treated, and the tutor only links a book when it really answers your question.
Talk now uses the same hold-to-talk box as Ask the tutor, so words you dictate are no longer cut off, and anything being read aloud pauses while you hold.
the page line at the foot of the reader ('Mark 12 · 12%', 'Page 2 of 7') is easier to tap with a thumb, and looks the same.
A Bible reference you share to Lampas opens a small pop-up with the verse in the way you are reading (English, Weave or Greek), and Open takes you to that verse in its chapter.
Tapping a Greek word now has a Paradigm row that opens that word's table with its own form outlined, and Back brings the word back.
Choose a book opens with the search box ready to type in and the keyboard up.
The help that opens under a setting now looks like a neat card instead of grey text with a bright yellow link.
the Greek voice now says εἰμι, ἐστιν and similar small words as one word (ee-mee) instead of spelling the letters.
Lampas remembers the Bible verses it found in a screenshot you shared, so going back for the next verse is instant and the picture is not read again.
Tap the chapter line at the foot of the reader to open the whole chapter with Listen, Read it aloud, Ask the tutor and Quiz me.
In Greek word order, a verse's full stop now stays at the end of the verse instead of appearing in the middle.
When you show interest in the Greek, the tutor now offers to turn up the Greek dial by one step, never more, and stays quiet about the Greek at Just English unless you ask.
Settings now opens with a "How much Greek?" dial, from Just English to All in, and each step shows only the Greek that step is about.
When the tutor says a second form of a word aloud, it no longer pronounces the rough breathing as an "h".
A long reading that is too slow to send on a weak connection now says so, instead of saying the tutor is offline.
A long reading now gets more time to be checked, and if it still takes too long you are told so instead of that the tutor is offline.
Settings has a Talk section where you choose whether the talk bars are held or tapped, and whether your words are sent when you let go or wait for the Send button.
Settings now opens on a short list of groups (Reading, Greek, The tutor, Listening, Daily, Study resources, Account), each its own page with a back arrow, and search still finds any setting.
The tutor no longer lists the Greek words you already know as words to learn when it only mentions them in passing.
Holding to talk now keeps your whole sentence when you pause in the middle, in every place you talk to the tutor.
The reading check now listens to a long reading for up to ten minutes instead of one, and if a reading is ever cut short it tells you where it stopped.
In Choose a book you can type just the start of a book's name, like "ep 4:15", and it finds Ephesians 4:15; typing a name's letters in order, like "phlm", finds the book too.
Sideways with the Immersive reader card showing, Turn pages now opens on page 1 with three lines of text instead of a sliver of 113 pages.
when your devotional is set to Random, asking the tutor for a different devotional now picks another one for today and keeps Random, and Settings has an Another button for it.
With the weave on, Read it aloud now lets you read the Greek words in Greek and the English words in English, and checks each word in its own language.
Quiz me no longer offers to keep a quiz goal you have already kept.
The chapter list no longer shows checkmarks or greys out the chapters you have finished; only the next chapter of your plan is outlined.
Choosing a verse like John 18:2 in Choose a book now opens that chapter in the Bible with the verse at the top, instead of the single-verse view.
The tutor can link you straight to John Calvin's commentaries or his Institutes in your Logos library when it talks about him: switch on the ones you own in Settings > Study resources > Works.
After you send a wish to the makers, a "Your requests" link beside "The answer will come back" takes you to the page where their answer appears.
In Turn pages the page now follows your finger and curls over like a real book page, springing back if you let go early and turning as fast as you flick it.
when your devotional is set to Random, Today now has an Another button that picks a different devotional for the day without leaving Random.
Review no longer says a drill is due when that drill has no questions to ask.
after you mark the Greek alphabet known, Settings > Grammar approach marks the first lesson after it as Next, not the letter Alpha.
A table you miss a form of in Review now comes back tomorrow even when you get the other forms right in the same round.
In Turn pages, turning past the last page of a chapter opens the next chapter, and turning back from the first page opens the end of the one before; no blank pages.

reloading the app while the Share to Lampas sheet is open keeps the sheet instead of dropping you on the reading screen, and a link that names Greek or English view keeps that view when the app was still starting.
The Chi and Gamma lessons now name the same letters before their soft sound as the drill's rule line does, instead of just "e and i".
A paradigm table with no form unlocked can no longer be put in Review, and a table that can't be asked is no longer counted as due.
Sharing only a GIF (or another file Lampas cannot read) to Lampas now just says it was left out and offers Cancel, instead of leading to an empty talk.
Tap to hear now says αυ, ευ and ηυ as one sound with a v or f (ηὐλίζετο is "eev-LEE-zeh-to"), not as two vowels.
after you mark The Greek alphabet known, the letters now show as Solid on the ladder graph and the tutor knows them, instead of showing as Next or Not yet.
Sending Audible a screenshot while the phone has no connection now says you are offline and offers Try again, instead of saying the screenshot could not be read.
With Immersive reader and Turn pages, the card now says to turn the page, and turning to the next page puts the bars away so the page has the whole screen.
The Weave you chose in Settings now stays on if the app reloads before you go back to reading.
Sharing a GIF to Lampas now tells you at once that only JPEG, PNG or WebP pictures can be read, instead of accepting it and refusing it in the talk.
Lesson sheets leave a strip of the screen above them again, so a tap there closes them.
tapping a locked form in Paradigms now offers a button for each idea it needs that opens that idea.
a long question you have pasted into Talk or Ask the tutor and not yet sent is still in the box when you close the sheet and open it again.
When you read a Greek verse aloud, the coach now uses the app's own syllables and stress for its tips instead of guessing.
an idea you were taught but never answered no longer says "last answered today" on its sheet; it says "not answered yet".
The passage you open from a section heading now sits on the page like the Reader's text, without a box drawn round it.
The Chi letter sheet now says in one sentence that χ has two sounds, hard before some letters and soft before e and i, with a word of each.
in Turn pages each page now fills down to the page line, without the blank band under the text.
Sharing a picture to Lampas now keeps the Bible references in your words when the picture cannot be read, and says so when the phone is offline.
The tutor's offers no longer show a change twice, a question you type is no longer treated as one you spoke, and the lesson you just started is no longer offered again.
After a drill, the results screen has an Ask the tutor button, and the tutor knows each question, what you answered and which answers were right or wrong.
The reader's switch now has English, Weave and Greek, and holding Weave flips the woven text between English and Greek word order.
Asking the tutor on a verse how to say a Greek word now gives the app's own syllables and stress, instead of the tutor guessing them.
Going back from a table to an idea's sheet now returns you to the place you were reading, not the top of the sheet.
The whole path is moved with your finger, a pinch or the arrow keys, and the clunky arrow and zoom buttons are gone, leaving one small Where I am button.
After you answer a Review or Quick test word, tap the verse reference under it to see that verse, with the word marked, in the way you read.
In Greek view the verse screen no longer offers an English audio Bible.
Read aloud no longer names the letter "delta" when a short elided word ends a Greek stretch before English words; it plays the sound instead.
Chi's card now names ω among the letters before the hard kh sound, as the drill's rule line does.
The letter sheets now show four different words as examples, instead of several forms of the same word.
A question to the tutor is no longer lost when you leave the page or the page reloads, a phone going offline is said at once, and after Send the question and the wait stay in view.
Reading a verse aloud no longer says the letter name "delta" for a word like δ' (Luke 9:24 and 24 other verses).
the sounds that change by position (ευ, αυ, ηυ as v or f, and γκ, μπ, ντ, γχ) now say when each sound is used, and their drills ask about real words with the pair marked instead of the pair alone.
A Greek word tapped on a letter or idea sheet now opens its word sheet in front, not hidden behind.
The Update ready and Welcome back bars no longer hide the top of the What's new sheet, a Bible reference card or the one-line speaker help.
holding δ' (δέ with its vowel dropped) now plays the th sound instead of the voice naming the letter.
A quick double tap on "Mark known without a drill" (or on "Show more" examples) on a grammar idea no longer lands on the control that moved into its place.
The letter sheets no longer offer cut-off words like δ' as examples, so the speaker says a real word instead of the letter's name.
When you ask the tutor in your own words how to say a Greek word, it now uses the app's own syllables and stress instead of guessing.
The Welcome back strip and the update bar no longer hide the top buttons of the verse screen or sit on top of the tutor's play bar.
On a phone with no Greek voice, a word list entry ending in ὁ now plays the sound of ὁ instead of naming the letter.
Offline, the sheet for a letter such as xi now says the examples could not be looked for, instead of saying no word is spelt with it.
on a small phone with larger text, the next word to practise is no longer hidden behind the Try again and Skip for now buttons.
Back from Placement's and a Paradigms table's top-left button now leaves the screen properly, so the phone's Back no longer returns to the screen you just left.
with Turn pages, a tap on the left edge of the text always turns back, even on a verse number, instead of opening that verse.
Tapping the middle of the 'Your level' slider no longer changes the level; only sliding it does.

A short box that cannot take all of what you paste now tells you how much was cut off; a question to the makers can be as long as a question to the tutor, and a server error shows 'The tutor is offline right now' instead of technical words.
reading aloud in Greek no longer says "omicron" for a one-letter word such as ὃ in the middle of a verse or a word list entry; it says the vowel's sound.
A paradigm table in Study mode no longer tells you to tap a cell when every cell is still locked; it says to mark the grammar ideas that open them.
A quick double tap on Read aloud, on 'Me' after a reading check, or on a marked word no longer undoes itself.
After you mark the Greek alphabet as known, Learn next and the list of gaps no longer name its letters.
With Turn pages on, closing Lampas or reloading it now opens the chapter on the page you were reading, not page 1.
An idea you put back to Not yet by switching now shows when it is next due and when you last answered it.
In Turn pages, coming back to the Reader from Settings or another screen now opens the page you were reading, not page 1.
Done on the Grammar sheet or the idea sheet now closes every sheet open over the page, the word card too, instead of leaving the card behind.
When the tutor fails while your phone is sideways, the error message and its Retry button now stay on the screen in every sheet.
Lampas at 200% text: the Greek alphabet's letter tiles, the 'Read Romans 8' heading, Drill it's 'Add πνεῦμα to my words' button and the Share screen spill or cut (left by mw-cwf538.10)
after the phone leaves full screen by itself in the Immersive reader, a two-finger tap on the text puts it full screen again.
In the Paradigms tables, a quick double tap on a padlocked form now keeps the explanation open instead of closing it again.
In Drill it, a right answer after a Hint now says it does not count toward Proved, and the next question asks the same kind of word again.
leaving the tutor's screen no longer loses an answer that was waiting for you; the "tap to play" bar stays until you play it.
With the Immersive reader on, reading aloud no longer slides the bars away by itself; only your own scrolling or a two-finger tap changes them.
Marking The Greek alphabet known now moves "Learning now" on to the next idea instead of leaving none.

At the largest text size, the titles and word meanings in the drills, the Check and Try it sheets, the Goal screen, the Hebrew guide and Ask for another approach are written out in full instead of ending in an ellipsis.
A quick double tap on Paradigms' Review mode, Hide all or a reveal cell, and on a tick box or switch elsewhere, now counts as one tap instead of undoing itself.
after Lampas reloads with a word card or grammar card open, the first Back press now leaves the page instead of doing nothing for each card that was open.
'Update ready, tap to reload' and the Welcome back strip can now be tapped when a verse or a sheet is open.

The Talk sheet now keeps a failed message, the Take me there button and the start of the answer on screen, also when the phone is turned, and a spoken question shows your own words under the tutor's tidied version.

A section heading's passage keeps the Reader's paragraphs and spacing; sideways the Audible link and the omicron sound are in view, the tutor-answered bar can be tapped, and the reading ladder says "Number N of M".
the back buttons at the top of a screen now step back, so the phone's Back leaves the screen instead of returning you to the one you just left.
A quick double tap on a link that opens another tab or app, such as 'Adopted in' under Your requests, now opens it once.
Tapping a locked form in the Paradigms tables now says what you need to learn first.
In the Immersive reader the place line now reads 100% when you reach the last verse, not only after the chapter buttons below it.
At the largest text size the reading bar is one row of icons, a passage's heading shows whole, and the book list no longer cuts off its title.
a quick double tap no longer acts twice; the second tap does nothing on the screen or sheet the first one opened, anywhere in the app.
Today's reading plan now lists the chapters you read today with a tick each, and a tick box beside the next chapter marks it read.
With the Immersive reader on in the Dark theme, the phone's top bar and the band behind the Talk button are now pure black like the page instead of dark blue.
Coming back to the Reader from Settings no longer hides the top and bottom bars when you have not scrolled.
On the reading plan you can now say where you are, by tapping the plan's next chapter on Today and choosing the chapter you are reading or any place you pick or type, with Undo for a few seconds.
Settings > Daily has a "Request a devotional" box where you can type the title of a devotional you own and send it to the makers.

The immersive reader's place line is easier to read and clears the phone's bottom bar, the text no longer jumps when the bars come back, the how-it-works card gets out of the way while you read, large type no longer opens wide gaps in the lines, the verse play buttons are dim, and full screen returns after the phone leaves it.
The whole path now has arrow buttons that move the graph, and tabbing to an idea brings it into view.
The About button and version line no longer sit at the bottom of every chapter; About is in Settings.
At the largest phone text size, the whole-path graph's labels now grow with the text, and the Talk screen and the passage view no longer cut off their titles and buttons.
Ask the tutor from Today and it knows which of the day's links you opened, and sending a screenshot of what you read is one tap.
The Reader has buttons, found with a keyboard or TalkBack, for what used to be gestures only: bring back or put away the bars, leave or start immersive reading, and turn a page.
'Link Logos in Settings' now opens Settings at Study resources even when you had left Settings scrolled down.
Lampas now reads Greek in a Greek voice under TalkBack, says out loud the tutor's answers, quiz results and reading marks, and moves TalkBack into a sheet when it opens and back when it closes.
The Reader's top row has a Today chip that shows how much of your day you have done and opens Today, replacing the separate Due and reading plan chips.
High contrast theme (white on black with thick outlines), and Lampas follows the phone's own text size up to 200% without cutting labels off.
A Today page gathers your due review, your reading plan's chapter, the day's Psalms and Proverbs and a devotional, each a tap away, with boxes you tick yourself. (Not yet reachable by a button.)
Text and buttons in the light and dark themes are a little easier to read, and the New words chip now reads "New 3 words" aloud.
typing a place such as John 18:36 in Choose a book now opens that chapter at that verse instead of saying no book matches.
Settings has a Daily section to choose what your daily list holds, which devotional it shows (or a random one), and whether it has tick boxes.
A quick double tap on 'Skip for now' in the Reading ladder no longer skips a verse you have not seen.
Read more's book links now open Logos at the lesson.
The settings search is now only on Settings, and it stays at the top while you scroll.
Review no longer asks to tap "the word that is plural singular" or "nominative negative"; each line names one number and one case at most.

eight more optional Hard sounds lessons, on γ, χ, δ and θ, π τ κ without a puff, pure vowels, κ γ χ λ before e and i, μπ ντ γκ, and two consonants at the start of a word, each with its tip for an American or a British ear, a listening drill and a verse from 1 John.
Review no longer asks the endings of third-declension nouns (πατήρ, φῶς, χείρ, σκότος) until The third declension has been opened, and 'See the table' now opens the right table.
Tapping the update banner now always reloads the app within a few seconds, instead of sometimes getting stuck on "Updating…".

Settings > Grammar approach now opens any lesson's idea sheet when you tap it, and a goal now teaches compound verbs, marks that change the word, enclitics and words that sound alike when its words show them.
an optional lesson, 'Rolling your r', on the Rho card for English speakers: from the tap in 'butter' to the Greek tapped r, with the trill as a stretch goal.
The Licence page now lists the devices on your licence by name and last use, and lets you rename one or remove it to free its place.
Search for any setting from any screen with the magnifier, and the tutor can send you straight to a setting.
The Licence page now explains what a licence unlocks and lets you get a free one with your email and phone number.
The augment card now says plainly which past verbs have the augment and that only the indicative has it.
In a Hard sounds lesson's 'Try it' step you can hold a button to say the word, then hear your try followed by the Greek voice.
the "Which idea is this?" card no longer gives away three answers by leaving the word "or" in the text.
in Drill it, a right answer after a Hint now says it does not count, so you know why you stay on the same step.
In a Hard sounds lesson, "Which did you hear?" plays a Greek word from a close pair, you tap which one it was over ten rounds, and a miss shows the pair side by side to hear again.
the card after 'Start from the letters' now shows the same solid, frontier and not-yet numbers as the Goal screen when some single letters are already solid.
Listening to a chapter outside your reading plan now opens Audible straight away, with no "tell me where you got to" prompts.
In the English view with the Weave on, each Greek word in a woven phrase like "ὑμῖν γράφω" opens its own word sheet and is read aloud on its own.
The Greek alphabet card now shows only words that have the look-alike letters it teaches, instead of unrelated words from the verse.
Missing a 'Words that sound alike' question now tells you the two words sound the same in Modern Greek and that the spelling is what tells them apart.
an optional 'Hard sounds' section on Goal, starting with a short lesson on the Greek tapped r, reachable from the Rho card too.
Searching Settings for 'Audible' or 'Word of Promise' now finds the Audio Bible setting.
the augment lesson now quotes a phrase that is really in 1 John 1:1.
Ask the tutor on Settings now remembers what you asked earlier in the talk, so a follow-up like "Here are the others" is answered in context.
the augment sheet now gives the same English for a word in its worked example and in its examples.
Stopping partway through a chapter in Audible no longer counts that chapter as done, so your next listen starts at the beginning of the chapter you stopped in.
You can now choose the typeface of the English text in Settings (Literata, Atkinson Hyperlegible, Lexend, or your phone's own), and the Greek and Hebrew stay as they are.
Tapping the tutor's offer of the Greek now says in the Talk sheet that it worked.
On Placement, 'Start from the letters' now names a few of the ideas you already have solid and counts the rest, so 'Back to the goal' stays on the phone's first screen.
the paradigm tables now show every Greek form whole, in its own cell and with readable row labels, at every text size.
Going Back from a verse opened from a shared Bible reference now returns to the Reader instead of the Share to Lampas sheet.
Words you type in the Quiz goal box in Settings and do not save are no longer lost when you leave Settings and come back.
In Settings, the Quiz goal no longer says 'Quiz goal' twice in a row; the line under the label now starts 'Kept:'.
A passage lesson now opens its verses with a short Lesson strip, and Check asks eight questions to pass it by reading, with Try again tomorrow in Review and the tutor's Quiz me if you miss.
a Turn pages choice in Settings > Reading lays a chapter out in pages that you turn with a tap at either side or a swipe, with the page number under the text.
Review now asks each preposition with a few different Greek phrases for every case, so a right answer shows you read the case and not just the phrase.
In Settings, the Quiz goal's Save button now looks plainly off when there is nothing new to save, and Clear no longer shifts sideways when Save turns on.
The Greek in the 'In Greek' paragraph of a Grammar sheet now shows in the Greek typeface like the rest of the Greek.
Start from the letters no longer tells you Learn next opens the Greek alphabet when you already know everything your goal needs.
Once you have the grammar a passage needs, the Goal screen now offers to read it ("Read 1 John 1:1-4") and Settings lists those reading lessons at the end of the grammar path.
In 1 John 2:6 the idea sheet for the aorist now shows "walked" for περιεπάτησεν instead of "walk".
Learn this idea on a preposition's Grammar sheet now opens that preposition's own lesson, such as περί, instead of the general lesson on prepositions.
the one-time licence tip now slides in and ignores taps for its first half second, so a late tip no longer catches a tap meant for the page.
Review now asks the sentence ideas on real verses, marking the words and asking what they are doing or which word they belong to.
The tutor now offers the Greek to a reader whose word list is still just the example words the app came with.
Settings now writes the name of the Audio Bible, Immersive reader card, Reading plan, Read aloud span, Read lessons to me and English accent choices above them.
Saying yes to 'Take me there' after you have already tapped it once now opens the lesson again.
The note about a licence no longer makes the free read-aloud sound like a paid extra.
The Goal screen now lists the sentence patterns a passage uses, such as a clause with ἵνα or the three kinds of "if", and each one's sheet shows your verses with those words marked.
The Greek word in a lesson's title, such as περί in 'The preposition περί', now shows in the same Greek letters as the rest of the lesson.
Settings has "Ask for more", where you can ask the tutor (or fill in a short form) for an approach, a study resource, a text or a translation Lampas does not have yet, and it goes to the makers.
Listen in Audible no longer takes the Lampas tab to audible.com; if no app takes it, the book page opens in a new tab and Lampas stays where it was.
Holding the Talk button no longer makes the phone chime at every pause while you speak, and the words after a pause still reach your question.
Open in Logos no longer replaces Lampas with a web page when the Logos app is not on the phone; the web page opens in its own tab.
In the tutor talk, after you tap an offered setting change while the answer is being read aloud, the 'Changed' line and Copy stay in view above the reading controls.

Each grammar idea now has a 'Try it on a verse' button that asks three short questions on the easiest verse you can read with that idea, then opens the verse for you to read; Review's questions about the passage also come from verses at your level.
the notice for a Bible reference that Lampas does not hold now names it the way the page you shared printed it.
Tapping a Bible reference twice quickly no longer makes its card vanish; the card stays up.
The Greek words in a Review question's sentence, and the Greek answer choices, are now drawn large in the Greek typeface.
Drill it now names the letter you misread in a word as a weak point, instead of saying Weak: none.
a quick double tap on Done or Drill it in a sheet no longer taps whatever is underneath, such as opening Settings or closing the sheet below.
after the tutor's offer to change a setting is tapped, the card no longer shows a stray second 'Changed' line.
the table for the verb οἶδα no longer has a column headed 'Greek'.
Tapping an Old Testament reference such as Gen. 1:28 in Share to Lampas now shows a "Not in Lampas yet" card (with Open in Logos) instead of jumping to Romans 8.
An optional course, Learn the IPA sounds, under Optional on the Goal screen, teaches the symbols for Greek's sounds with a drill and a pass check; nothing else in the app needs it.
After a partly read verse, the word you stopped at is now underlined in the verse, and tapping it takes you to the Next word box.
Under Grammar books in Settings you can now ask for another grammar book from your Logos library; the request goes to the makers, and if you are offline it waits and goes when you are back online.
A Review round you leave mid-way, by reloading or by the phone dropping the page, now picks up at your next question instead of going back to Start.
a wrong answer on a Movable letters card in Review now says why in one short line (consonant, smooth or rough breathing), not only the right answer.
Write it now shows where to start each stroke of a letter, in what order and which way to go, with a short line saying how many strokes.
the English beside each example word on a grammar idea's page is shown in full, no longer cut short with '…'.
after you open the chapter the tutor offered, Talk no longer keeps saying it was not opened or offering the button.

The Bible view has a Plan chip showing the next chapter you will listen to and how far you are, and the chapter picker marks the chapters you have done and the next one; you start a listening plan from the chip or from Settings.
A lesson's example word never shows a meaning that repeats itself, such as 'to see: see'.
See the whole path draws every grammar idea as a map, with what you know, what you are learning and what comes next, that you can drag and zoom, opened from the Goal screen.
On About, the Preface and Your requests buttons no longer have their small description line pressed against the bottom edge.
Back from Audible, you can send a screenshot of Audible's playing screen and Lampas reads which chapter you reached; one tap accepts it.
the Next word box no longer shows a one-syllable word twice.
in the 'Which fits?' cards for words told apart by their marks, no wrong choice means the same as the right one any more.
reloading the placement's 'Where you are' card, or going Back to it from the Goal screen, now shows the card again instead of starting over.
Review now says it is getting your questions while a round loads on a slow connection, instead of showing a blank screen.
Write it no longer says Right when you write a Latin y, k, x, u or dotted i for the Greek letter; it says Close and tells you where it differs.
On Your requests, a tap on a long request now shows all of it, and a second tap folds it again.
A paused reading no longer shows a stop square on its speaker, as if it were still playing.
the Greek alphabet's worked example now gives each letter's sound as well as its name.
the Talk sheet's title is no longer cut short on a phone held upright; it wraps onto a second line instead.
with Logos on, an idea sheet's Read more links straight to the lesson that teaches it in Black's Learn to Read New Testament Greek, and Settings lets you tick which grammar books to show.
a quick double tap on Back to the goal after a placement no longer opens the Goal screen's ideas list.
Swiping to the next or previous chapter in the Immersive reader no longer flashes the title bar and bottom bar.
Help text in Settings and the notes that show after an update now have a speaker button, so you can hear them read aloud.
Held sideways, the note about a licence is now one slim row at the foot instead of nearly half the screen.
In American English, the example words for π, τ and κ are now spin, stop and skate, said without the puff of breath that Greek does not have.
Back from Audible, Lampas now asks where you got to in the plan and suggests the chapter from how long you were away.
When the tutor is down and your phone is online, Ask the tutor and Talk now say the tutor is offline instead of telling you to check your connection.
Drill it on a letter no longer asks the same word twice in one drill after you tap Hint, when your chapter has another word with that letter.
Your requests now checks for news as soon as you come back to the app, instead of up to 20 seconds later.
the fill-in-the-ending question now shows the movable ν in brackets for ἐστίν and for dative plurals like πᾶσιν, as it already did for -σιν endings.
the parts of the tutor answer time on About now add up exactly to the total.
a Sepia theme in Settings > Appearance, with warm paper and dark brown text for long reading.
tapping Reading ladder now shows 'Loading the ladder…' at once instead of seeming to do nothing while the list loads.
the Next mark in Settings under Grammar approach now names the same lesson as Learn next on the Goal screen.
Double-tapping the close button of the licence tip no longer opens a word sheet by accident.
The letters Write it shows you now join up like real handwriting, so alpha is one smooth stroke instead of a bowl and a separate slash with a gap.
The "A verb with no voice" question now reads as plain English, with the blank where the name was.
a quiet update that arrives while you are reading now finishes the next time you leave the app, instead of waiting for the next restart.
a reading sent over a slow link that the tutor received late is now answered, instead of showing 'Could not reach the tutor' and sending it twice on Retry.
The Accents and stress lesson now says how the stress is said in the Greek pronunciation you chose, under How it sounds.
In the Quick test, while the answered word speaks by itself, Tap to hear shows the stop square and one tap stops it.
a grammar idea's example words now show at the top of its sheet, all in view when it opens, upright or sideways, with 'Show N more' when there are more than three.
a word's sheet shows the English it stands for without the verse's full stop, comma or quotes.
The tutor's switch to Typing or Speaking now takes even when it sent another change the app ignores.
For an American reader, the sound of chi is now keyed to "chutzpah", the throaty ch, instead of "loch", which many Americans say as "lock".
In Drill it, missing a "How is this word said?" question now asks the same letter again with a different word, instead of ending the drill on an easier question.
Tapping an Old Testament chapter now lets you choose between reading it in Logos or listening to it in Audible.
The third declension sheet no longer lists οὐδεμία, which belongs to the first declension, as one of its examples.
Holding to talk on an Android phone no longer shows a "language-not-supported" error when the phone could have heard you another way.
After a Review round, Lampas quietly asks the tutor for fresh questions on the grammar you missed, ready for your next round.
The letter drill now asks you to say a letter's name or sound aloud and checks it with your phone's speech recognition; a miss plays the right sound.
About now thanks Biblical Mastery Academy and links to their course and community for anyone who wants a teacher.
A quick double tap on Next in the grammar drills no longer uses up your Hint, skips a word, closes the result or leaves for the tutor.
When you paste a long question or prayer to the tutor, it now keeps all of it and does not cut it after the first line.

once a pen has touched the screen, each letter's lesson and the letter drill let you write the letter by hand (trace, then copy, then from memory), checked on the phone, with a Handwriting drills switch in Settings.
reading a verse aloud with Greek words woven in no longer marks the Greek words you read in Greek as missed, and the panel says it can check English only.
a Greek word you tap to hear is now said with its stress where the respelling shows it, and Settings names your Greek voice and lets you test it.
One path: Lampas now teaches by its own ladder for everyone. Thank you, Biblical Mastery Academy, for the inspiration (see About).
'Listen in Audible' now opens the Audible app and plays from the start of the chapter you are reading.
The pluperfect table now gives you one set of endings, so ἐλελύκειμεν and ἐλελύκειτε agree with οἶδα's ᾔδειμεν and ᾔδειτε.
The tutor no longer asks again what you are learning Greek for after you have said you would rather not say.
fifty more of the New Testament's commonest words now have a memory picture beside them on Words and in the Quick test.
Drill it no longer asks the same word twice when your reading goal has no word with the letter you are drilling.
Review can ask you to parse a whole word step by step, and to tap who does the action, what is done and what it is done to in a verse.
after a partly read verse, the next word to practise is now always fully visible above the buttons instead of hidden behind them.
a Weave setting 'Order' lays the woven verse out in the Greek word order, with the English of the other words where their Greek stands.
Review now asks what a phrase of a verse says, showing the Greek and four English choices taken from the verse itself.
a Greek word of one letter, like ὁ, now sounds in your phone's own Greek voice instead of a robotic clip, and the letter drills say a vowel's sound.
on a phone whose clock is ahead, About's 'Last tutor answer' no longer shows a wait longer than the whole answer, and its parts add up to the total.
Word meanings no longer show the dictionary's shorthand: πνεῦμα reads "spirit, breath" and ἐν reads "in, by, with (dative)".
Settings has an English accent choice (American, British or IPA) that changes every sound hint at once, and the tutor knows which you chose.
Moving The Greek alphabet to Learning now starts a letter drill: all 24 letters, small and capital, heard or named, in rounds until each is right.
With the Immersive reader on, turning to the next or previous chapter now keeps the bars hidden instead of bringing them back.
Play my reading now starts right where your voice starts, skipping the silence before your first word.
on Share to Lampas, a double tap on Page order, Bible order or Choose a talk no longer opens a reference or picks a talk by mistake.
In the evening, the Memory page wrote tomorrow's date beside your 'no' to learning Greek; it now writes today's.
The passage view of a heading now shows its verses in the same type and spacing as the Reader.
Lessons can now read themselves aloud when they open, if you turn on 'Read lessons to me' in Settings; the words stay on screen.
A table of forms can be put in Review, which asks you for its forms one by one by their grammatical names.
Talk and Ask now keep and send a long pasted prayer or passage, up to 4000 characters, instead of cutting it off.
A grammar idea now links to its table, and Review asks you for an ending only after you have opened the table that shows it.
After a few visits, Lampas shows a free reader one quiet line, once, about what a licence adds, and it is easy to find out how to get one.
Ask the tutor, with the phone held sideways, shows the question and its Copy button on one line, so more of the answer is in view.
Three Logos lexicon buttons on the word sheet now show the book's name instead of a code.
A letter's example words now really make the sound the card teaches, simple words come first, and a different sound in a pair is shown on purpose.
the Talk message box no longer squeezes to one letter wide with the keyboard up, grows upward as you type, and "Hold to talk" no longer has a notch cut out of it.
A new install of Lampas now starts empty instead of with the app owner's own words and progress, and Words points a new reader to Placement and Import.
The Paradigms screen now has tables for the subjunctive, imperative, infinitive and participle, and εἰμί's moods, each unlocking as you learn the grammar behind it.
Scrolling Settings with your thumb over a speed slider no longer changes your Greek or English speed.
the tutor's Sound it out help no longer adds an "h" for a rough breathing in Modern Greek.
In the letter sound questions, every choice is now one short sound like 'o, as in “or”, short', never a rule or a long aside.
The Paradigms screen now has tables for the future, aorist, perfect, contract and -μι verbs and οἶδα, with each form's tense sign or augment named.
Back from a word opened inside a letter or idea sheet now returns to that sheet instead of jumping out to the Goal screen.
A reader who chose English no longer gets a Greek word card when asking what an English word like "love" means.
Listen in Audible: turn on the Audio Bible in Settings and a verse's Listen opens The Word of Promise in Audible and tells you which chapter to pick.
The Paradigms screen now has tables for the third declension, adjective endings, the personal pronouns, this and who, and the question and "someone" pronouns.
The example words on the grammar sheets no longer show a neighbouring word's English, so περί reads 'about' and ἐψηλάφησαν reads 'touched'.
A grammar lesson question now uses only the words you have already been taught, such as 'Tap the singular noun' instead of 'Tap the accusative singular personal pronoun'.
The sound of o (omicron and omega) is now explained with the o of "or", said short, which fits an American ear, instead of "lot".
A reader who has said no to the Greek no longer gets Greek words in the tutor's answer when he asks what an English word means.
A small speaker button on the grammar and idea lessons, new-word cards, the tutor's answers and What's new reads the text aloud with your phone's voice, Greek in Greek, and a second tap stops it.

The grammar ladder now teaches how Greek words are built (stems and endings, the three declensions, the augment, tense signs, contract and -μι verbs, εἰμί and οἶδα), and a passage you are reading tells you which of these its words use.
Drill it now takes its words from the chapter you are reading toward, and does not show the same word twice in one drill.
after you answer a question in Review, the Quick test, the Parsing drill or Placement, the Next button stays in view at the bottom of the screen, with no scrolling.
When the verse you are reading has no word showing a letter or idea, its card now takes examples from the nearby section, the chapter or the book, and says where they come from.
A new reader is welcomed by the tutor in plain English, with a few short questions that set up Lampas for them, and can skip them.
Drill it on a sound that changes with the next letter (like χ, kh or hy) now asks words of both kinds, offers the same word said the other way as a wrong answer, and names the rule when you miss.

every grammar card now teaches from scratch: what the idea is, how to spot it with a table of its endings, and a word from your verse taken apart step by step, and its examples are only words the card can explain.
When the tutor shows how a Greek word sounds, reading it aloud now says the Greek sound instead of spelling out the letters.
A long spoken question to the tutor, or a large word list, no longer fails with "This grist is too large to send".
a Greek word of one letter, such as Ὃ or ὁ, now sounds as its vowel, not as the letter's name "omicron".
In a Talk, each of your own questions now has a Copy button, so a question that is too long to send can be copied whole and trimmed elsewhere.
When the tutor is down, the app now says the tutor is offline instead of blaming your connection.
You now learn one grammar idea at a time: Goal says what you are learning now, and a new idea starts only when you finish the one before or you choose to switch.

A verse from the Old Testament in the tutor's answer now opens in your Logos, in the Bible you chose, and if Logos is not linked it takes you to where to link it.
Back on the word, grammar and idea cards now goes back one step at a time, to the last place you were, instead of skipping some.
Your requests now has a back button that returns to About when you came from About, and a double tap on a back button no longer jumps you two screens.
Share a screenshot of a book page to Lampas and it lists the Bible references on it as links.
Switching the Greek pronunciation now starts the letters, sounds and marks again in the new one and keeps your old progress, ready for when you switch back.
after you say yes or no to sending an idea to the makers, the 'Sent' or 'Not sent' mark stays in view next to the tutor's reply.
The Quiz goal label in Settings is now bold, and the Save button looks plainly greyed out when there is nothing to save.
The Greek voice now says the n in words like Πάντοτε, as the line under the word shows, and χ is spelt KH or HY (χαίρετε is HYE-re-te) to match how it sounds.
After a drill that shows what you are weak at, Lampas makes you a short plan of drills on those points, easiest first, brings them up in Review, and ends with a drill that proves the idea.
Share text to Lampas and it lists every Bible reference in it as a tappable link that opens the verse, in the order of the page or in Bible order.
Example words on the grammar sheets now show their meaning as it stands in the verse (these things), not the dictionary meaning of the base word.
With Immersive reader on, the screen stays awake while you read.
the round Ask button no longer covers answers in Quick test or help text in Settings; every screen keeps room for it.
The "Which idea is this?" question no longer gives away its answer by naming the idea in other words.

When you come back after a break, the tutor now notices the words and ideas you have gone rusty on and offers to move them back to Frontier and practise, and a Welcome back card offers a short refresher.
A question you spoke but kept unsent (slid off the bar, or switched away from the app) and then sent is now treated as spoken, so the tutor hears through sound-alike words.
The Placement screen now says plainly that 'Start from the letters' is for someone who cannot yet read Greek, so a beginner does not take the quiz by mistake.
An idea's sheet now has a level slider (Not yet, Learning, I know it); sliding to I know it starts Drill it, which has to prove you know the idea, and the result shows where you are strong and weak.
In the Immersive reader a small quiet line at the bottom now shows the book, the chapter and how far through it you are, like a Kindle.
A quiet update that did not get applied the first time you left the app is now tried again the next time you leave it.
In the Immersive reader, Chrome's "To exit full screen" notice now shows once when you start reading, not after every two-finger tap.
A short reading hold is no longer sometimes mistaken for a tap when the phone's clock jumps back.
Without a licence the verse sheet no longer offers Read it aloud, its Hold to read bar or the Reading ladder (which could only end in 'No licence').
With Immersive reader on, the text is set like a book: tight lines in a serif typeface, even edges with hyphenation, pure black in the dark theme and small dim verse numbers.
The letters, sounds and marks cards now show their letters, vowel pairs, consonant pairs and marks as tiles you can tap to hear, each with its name and sound, instead of only describing them.
The lessons now teach when σ sounds like z, when αυ and ευ sound like v or f, where a breathing is written, and a new lesson 'Words that sound alike' with a hear-and-pick question.
With Immersive reader On, the Reader now fills the whole phone screen, hiding the status and navigation bars, as soon as you tap or scroll the text.
When you read in English, the tutor now answers in English and, if you show interest in the original, offers the Greek once with a button, and remembers if you say no.

the Breathing marks lesson now teaches Modern Greek sounds (breathings are silent, ὁ is “o”) instead of the old school pronunciation.
'Start from the letters' on Placement now counts the grammar you already have and names the idea Learn next will open, instead of saying you are starting from nothing.

Lampas no longer re-downloads the chapters you have already read each time the app updates, only a chapter whose text actually changed.
Sending an offer to the makers by tapping the button and saying yes no longer delivers it twice.
Changed: Hearing a word on the Quick test, flashcards and grammar questions is now one tap on 'Tap to hear' (tap again to stop), no longer a hold.

Settings has a Memory page where you can keep, edit, export and import notes that Lampas will later share with your tutor.
a one-letter Greek word such as Ὃ or ὁ is said by the Greek voice as its sound, not by the English voice.

About now shows how long your last tutor answer took, and how much of that was your phone, the network and the factory.

the tutor's answer no longer starts speaking while you are in another app; it waits and shows 'The tutor answered: tap to play' at the top when you return.
Lampas now opens for anyone without a licence, and a shared verse link opens for everybody.
The tutor's answer now shows within seconds of being ready, instead of waiting up to a minute or more on mobile data.

Two new grammar lessons, 'Marks that change the word' and 'Enclitics', teach the pairs of Greek words that differ only by a breathing or an accent, and the accents lesson now says where the marks matter.
The tutor now names a Greek word's dictionary form and meaning from the app's own word data, so it no longer swaps in a look-alike word such as τέκνον for τεκνίον.
A sound or word you keep missing when you read aloud now gets a short drill with the thing to remember and five practice words, and comes back in Review.
The grammar lessons now teach each common preposition one by one, with its meaning for each case and a real verse, and a lesson on verbs built from a preposition.
Learn next on the Goal screen now names the same gaps as the end card and Review, such as the rough breathing, and shows them even when no goal is set.
In immersive reading the top and bottom bars no longer come back by themselves at the end of a chapter; only a two-finger tap shows them or puts them away.
Read it aloud now grades a reading you stop part-way through, as far as you got, and helps you with the next word so each try goes further.
Greek words you say out loud to the tutor are now matched to the words of the verse, and the tutor tells you which word it took.
Holding a one-letter Greek word such as Ὃ or ὁ now says its sound instead of the letter's name.
The lessons on pairs of vowels, pairs of consonants and breathings now give each sound an English example word (e as in pet) and say they follow Modern Greek.
Sound it out now explains Greek sounds the modern way (αυ is "af" or "av", not "aw") and never splits a vowel pair.
A new lesson, Movable letters, teaches the little letter changes in Greek (the ν that comes and goes, οὐ/οὐκ/οὐχ, ἐκ/ἐξ), and the ending questions now show that ν in brackets.
The tutor now knows your words and grammar when it checks your reading and when it offers a tip, and every answer is pitched to what you told it in About you.
The sheet for letters, vowel pairs, breathings and accents now shows words from your verse with the letters it teaches marked.
Sound it out now says a one-letter syllable by its sound instead of the letter's name.
the "Which idea is this?" grammar question no longer gives away its own answer.
Settings now has an "About you" page where you can tell the tutor your age, pace, how you learn best, your background and why you are learning Greek, so its answers meet you where you are.
Read it aloud now has a Reading ladder that starts at the easiest verse to pronounce, keeps your place separately for Greek and English, and offers the next verse after a good reading.
When you switch on the immersive reader, a small card now tells you how to bring the bars back and how to leave, and you can tell it not to show again.
Lampas no longer asks you to update for a build with nothing new to show; such updates install quietly when you are not using it.
The grammar lessons now come in an order where nothing is taught before the grammar it relies on: singular and plural, and the little words and, but and not, come right after the noun.
Changed: In the Immersive reader the bars no longer come back when you scroll up; tap the text with three fingers (or two) to bring them back or send them away.
Read it aloud no longer says it could not reach the tutor when your connection drops for a moment; it keeps waiting for the answer.
Holding a Greek word that is a capital letter or a single letter now says the word instead of 'capital'.
A total beginner can start from the letters, and every goal now teaches the vowel and consonant pairs, syllables, the iota under a letter and punctuation before the grammar.
In Quiz me, the question about your quiz goal and its two buttons no longer slip out of sight when you turn the phone or the microphone message appears.
Telling the tutor to send a request to the makers, by tapping or by saying yes at the same moment, now sends it only once.
Your requests shows what became of each idea you sent (filed, being built, adopted in a version with a link, declined with a reason, or now a setting), and the tutor can tell you too.
The chapter title in the header is no longer cut off, the tutor says "Already on" when asked for the chapter you are on, and an answer that comes after you close Talk offers to open the chapter.
The tutor can now tell you what became of the ideas you sent to the makers, and offer to switch on one that became a setting.
Held sideways, the Reader now shows much more of the text, with the Ask button beside it.
In Settings, the Quiz goal now has a clear label and shows your goal, and Save stays off until you have typed something.

Settings and About now have "Your requests", which lists what you asked the factory for and shows whether it was filed, is being built, was adopted in a version (with a link), declined with a reason, or became a setting.
The Quiz me goal question now always shows with its Yes, from now on and Just this time buttons, in view without scrolling.
Review's final score now says 'Score' so it is not mistaken for the question counter, and sideways the answer options no longer sit under the Ask button.
Asking the tutor to take you to a chapter now works from every screen, not only the Reader.
When you tap Start over in the placement, its question and both answers now fit on screen (even sideways) and only Keep my answers is highlighted.
Held sideways, the Reader's Talk bar now fits whole on the screen.
The question shown above the tutor's answer no longer keeps stray "um" and "uh" from what you said.
You can now answer the tutor's offers by voice: say yes, no or 'read it back' instead of tapping Send this to the makers or a setting change.
Greek words in Robinson's essay use the app's Greek type.
Quiz me asks what you want from the quiz, and can keep it as your default.
Ask the tutor in landscape: the answer now has room to be read, and Hold to ask and Type a question share one row.
the Unlock screen has room above the icon again.
Review's 'Another round' no longer turns into a round of dozens of questions; a round stays at ten.
Tapping Place me twice quickly no longer throws away the placement you had started, and Start over now asks before it does.
Ask the tutor to take you to a chapter ("switch to Colossians 1") and the Reader opens there.
the Reader's Talk bar fits on a sideways phone.
The tutor's answer always shows, even when a setting he asked to change cannot be changed.
Tapping Next twice quickly in the Quick test no longer opens the Parsing drill by accident.
Ask the tutor brings the answer into view when it comes, and fits in landscape.
Tapping outside the Hebrew word's 'How to say it' sheet no longer ends the tutor's spoken answer; Resume stays.
the Unlock screen on a short or sideways phone no longer cuts off its top; you can scroll to all of it.
Review now asks the letters and letter pairs you were told to work on first, including ones you were never asked.
Read aloud on Robinson's essay no longer reads the footnote numbers.
Share a picture, text or link to Lampas from another app, and choose which tutor talk it goes to.
Hear a word says the right sound even when the tip first names the wrong one.
after twenty placement questions you can now go back to the Goal screen, and 'Go on another day' returns to where you started instead of Settings.
Ask the tutor is usable with the phone held sideways: the questions can be tapped and an answer has room to be read.
The unlock screen shows this phone's key as a QR code for Postern to scan.
The Robinson essay in the Preface is now the text from the 2005 edition's appendix, which is the version the edition released into the public domain, and the page says so.
In Ask the tutor, the other suggested questions stay after the first question, and a new 'New talk' button starts the talk afresh.
Tapping Next twice quickly in the placement, Review and the Quick test no longer answers the next question for you.
the arrows on a passage now carry on into the chapter before or after instead of stopping at the chapter's end.
In the Reader you can swipe left for the next chapter and right for the previous one, and at the first and last chapter a short note tells you there is no more.
Ask by in Settings lets you choose whether Ask the tutor starts with speaking or typing, and you can ask the tutor to switch it for you.
You can send the tutor a screenshot, a photo or a copied picture in a talk, and the Greek words it quotes are tap-to-hear.
An 'Immersive reader' setting lets the top and the Talk button slide away while you read, and come back when you scroll up a little or tap the text with two fingers.
Asking the tutor about a verse now uses the same big hold-to-talk bar as Postern, with your words showing as you speak and a quiet "Type a question" beneath it.
a word you read right twice now becomes solid even if your phone's clock was set back in between.
Robinson's essay on why he holds the Byzantine text to be original can now be read inside the app, on the Preface, in large type with its footnotes.
the tutor that helps fill in a form now asks just one question at a time, with nothing tacked on after it.
Listening to a passage now starts with one tap on Play, reads on by itself with Pause, Restart and Stop, and pauses and carries on when you ask the tutor, long-press a word or leave the screen.
The English word at the top of a word sheet no longer slides half under the tip card when the sheet is scrolled.
Tap a Bible reference in the tutor's answer to see the verse in a small card first, then open it in the reader.
The Reading check's speaker now says a word the way its tip spells it, so 'Levites' is said LEE-vites.
With many Logos lexicons switched on, the word sheet shows every one, each named in full, with a "More below" hint and a Close button at the bottom within thumb reach.
About, the Preface and My study way can now be read aloud to you and shared as a link from their top bar.
When the tutor names a New Testament verse in an answer, such as Hebrews 7:2, you can tap it to open that verse, and the tutor now answers questions about other passages right there.
Due, Goal, tip and new-word notices in the Reader now sit in one thin row of small buttons under the header, so the reading starts higher on the screen.
When the tutor is reading an answer, a tapped word or holding to talk now pauses him, and 'Resume' goes on from where he stopped, with 'Restart' and 'Stop' beside it.
The gaps between words in the Reader are now an even single space instead of wide, uneven gaps.

Turning Logos or Accordance on in Settings no longer opens the app or switches itself off; it stays on and offers a Get button if you don't have the app.
Every question and answer from the tutor now has a Copy button that puts the whole exchange on your clipboard as Markdown, with a link to the verse.
On the About screen you can now ask the tutor what any credit is, what it gives you and what its licence lets us do, or why we credit them all.
On the Ask for another approach form, a button now lets the tutor take you through it one question at a time, asking for a photo when it is needed and filling in the boxes as you answer.
the round Ask the tutor button no longer covers the end of the lines you are reading.
In the reading check, 'Me' now stops at the end of the flagged word instead of running on into the next words, and a word's comma stays with it.
the Logos buttons for three dictionaries that have no entry for a name no longer open a wrong page for names such as Melchizedek.
Everything Lampas reads aloud now has a Pause, Resume, Restart and Stop bar that remembers where you were, and leaving a screen pauses the reading.
The tutor now shows your question back with proper punctuation and capitals, with the ums and false starts taken out.
Holding 'Hold to ask' on a verse now shows what you say in the question box as you speak, and your question stays on screen until the tutor answers.
The placement test now checks your letters, letter pairs and breathing marks one by one, says which ones you still need, and Review asks them first.
What's new in the app
Lampas now works out which Greek letters, sounds and marks you know from the words you read right, so the Goal screen names only the letters you still need instead of the whole alphabet.
The Due strip's checks no longer fail when the computer is busy.
Every Logos link on the word sheet now opens the right entry.
The app's tests now use more realistic stand-ins for speech and the microphone.
